input.quote: 10. NONASSIGNABILITY. Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld.
input.rationale: Section 10 is the only assignment provision; there is no change-of-control language anywhere and no Vendor termination or re-pricing right on our change of control (Section 6 contains only mutual convenience and breach terminations), so the walk-away trigger is not present. However, the clause subjects every assignment, including an assignment to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, to the other party's prior consent. It therefore fails the fallback position, which requires a mutual successor-assignment right exercisable on written notice, even though it already satisfies the fallback's consent and reasonableness elements for other assignments. We propose the shortest fix at the fallback level: a mutual successor carve-out on written notice, leaving the consent standard intact for all other assignments (no affiliate exception is added, consistent with the fallback).

ops.text: Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may assign this Agreement to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all of its assets upon written notice to the other party.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a mutual successor-assignment right on written notice, so neither party can block a merger or asset sale; consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) continues to apply to all other assignments.
